question: Walk me through Django's complete request-response lifecycle.
title: Django Request-Response Lifecycle
direct_answer: Request enters WSGI/ASGI server → Django WSGIHandler/ASGIHandler → middleware chain (process_request on each) → URL dispatcher → view function → middleware chain reversed (process_response) → response. Middleware can short-circuit at any point. The ORM hits the database inside the view. Context processors add variables to all template contexts. Session middleware reads/writes sessions around the view. Exception middleware catches view exceptions.
interviewer_intent: Tests whether the candidate understands the full stack beyond just writing views — crucial for debugging, custom middleware, and performance optimization.

sections.title: Request lifecycle step by step
sections.content:
1. Web server (nginx/gunicorn): receives HTTP request, hands to WSGI callable.
2. Django WSGIHandler.get_response(): orchestrates the pipeline.
3. Middleware chain (forward): each middleware's process_request() runs. Security middleware checks HTTPS, auth middleware loads the user, session middleware loads the session. Any middleware can return a response early (short-circuit).
4. URL resolver: ROOT_URLCONF → URLconf → reverse URL matching → calls the view.
5. View: your code runs. Queries models. Returns HttpResponse (or raises an exception).
6. Exception handling: if the view raises Http404, PermissionDenied, or other exceptions, Django's exception middleware converts them to appropriate responses.
7. Middleware chain (reverse): each middleware's process_response() runs in reverse order. CSRF middleware validates tokens, gzip middleware compresses, cache middleware stores response.
8. Response sent back to web server, then to client.

Template rendering happens inside the view (render() call), not in the middleware chain. Context processors add to every template context just before render().

sections.title: Custom middleware example
sections.content:
# Writing middleware
class RequestTimingMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, get_response):
        self.get_response = get_response   # called once at startup

    def __call__(self, request):
        # Code here runs before the view
        import time
        start = time.perf_counter()

        response = self.get_response(request)   # calls the next middleware/view

        # Code here runs after the view
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        response['X-Request-Time'] = f'{elapsed:.4f}'
        return response

# settings.py
MIDDLEWARE = [
    'django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware',
    'django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware',
    'django.middleware.common.CommonMiddleware',
    'django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware',
    'django.contrib.auth.middleware.AuthenticationMiddleware',
    'django.contrib.messages.middleware.MessageMiddleware',
    'myapp.middleware.RequestTimingMiddleware',  # custom
]

# Middleware order matters:
# SecurityMiddleware first: redirects HTTP → HTTPS before anything
# SessionMiddleware before Auth: auth needs session
# CSRF before views: validates before view runs

sections.title: Lifecycle rules
items: Middleware runs forward on request, reverse on response
Any middleware can short-circuit by returning a response directly
AuthenticationMiddleware sets request.user before the view
Context processors run at template render time, not request time
Middleware __init__ runs once at startup; __call__ runs per request

seo.metaTitle: Django Request-Response Lifecycle — Middleware, URL Dispatch, Views
seo.metaDescription: Complete Django request lifecycle: WSGI handler, middleware chain, URL resolver, view execution, reverse middleware, and response. Includes custom middleware example.

speakable_v2.hook: The Django request lifecycle is a pipeline — middleware wraps the view like layers of an onion, and knowing this is essential for debugging and performance work.

beats.content: Request enters through the WSGI server, passes through each middleware's process_request (security checks, session loading, auth), then reaches the URL dispatcher which routes to your view. The view runs. Then middleware unwinds in reverse — CSRF validation, response compression, caching.
Any middleware can return a response early. SecurityMiddleware redirects to HTTPS before the URL dispatcher even runs. Authentication middleware can redirect unauthenticated users before the view.

Custom middleware is a callable. __init__ gets get_response (next in chain) once at startup. __call__ is per-request: run before-view code, call get_response for the rest of the pipeline, run after-view code on the response.

speakable_v2.cap: Middleware order in settings.py matters. SessionMiddleware must come before AuthenticationMiddleware because auth reads from the session.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with Django's CSRF protection mechanism, or how to add a per-request transaction boundary in middleware.
